subject: Fintro — schedule capacity sizing + demo
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@fintro.com>, Samantha Wu <samantha.wu@fintro.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fintro — schedule capacity sizing + demo

Hi Liam / Samantha —

Great to meet the team earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery: Fintro wants to run high-volume document ingestion for fraud-detection pipelines (real-time scoring + nightly batch re-embed), with peaks during business hours and occasional batch spikes at end-of-day. You mentioned current peak traffic is in the low thousands QPS for scoring requests and that latency sensitivity is primarily for the 99th percentile.

Next step: we'd like to lock a focused 60-minute capacity sizing + technical deep-dive with our infra team. Goal for that call: align on throughput profile (steady vs burst), target p99 latency, tokenization/sequence length assumptions, and whether you want dedicated Redwood capacity or a hybrid (hosted with reserved burst).

Proposed agenda (60 minutes):
- 5m quick intros and success criteria
- 20m current load profile & latency targets (you)
- 25m technical walkthrough of throughput/latency tradeoffs + dedicated sizing recommendations (us)
- 10m next steps / mutual action items

I've attached a short "Redwood sizing prep" doc that lists the fields we'd like you to share before the call (qps by route, typical sequence lengths, TTL/KV cache expectations). If you can send the current QPS export and SLO doc ahead of time, that will help us come prepared.

Proposed time windows (PDT):
- Thu Jul 8, 11:00–12:00
- Thu Jul 8, 14:00–15:00
- Fri Jul 9, 09:30–10:30

Can you confirm which slot works and who from your side should join (ops, infra, product)? Once we lock, we will send a calendar invite and a one-page pre-read.

Thanks —

David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[d] +1 415-555-0123 | david.kim@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-sizing-prep.pdf (1 page)

From: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@fintro.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Wu <samantha.wu@fintro.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fintro — schedule capacity sizing + demo

Thanks David — appreciate the clear agenda. Thu Jul 8 at 14:00–15:00 PDT works best for us. Samantha (ops lead) will join plus one of our infra engineers (Tariq).

I've attached a quick export of our recent scoring traffic and our internal SLO doc. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Peak sustained QPS for scoring routes today is ~1,800 QPS during US market open, with short bursts up to ~3,200 QPS for 30–90s during heavy validation windows.
- Typical sequence length for scoring payloads is ~320 tokens after tokenization; batch re-embed jobs average 2,400 tokens per request but run off-peak.
- For latency, our business team wants p99 under 250ms for scoring responses (including model processing only — network hops are separate).

Files attached: fintro-current-qps.csv, fintro-slo-requirements.pdf

We can add any other telemetry you need. Looking forward to the call.

— Liam
Liam O'Neil
Head of Product | Fintro
liam.oneil@fintro.com
Attachment: fintro-current-qps.csv (CSV, 2.1MB)
Attachment: fintro-slo-requirements.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@fintro.com>, Samantha Wu <samantha.wu@fintro.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fintro — schedule capacity sizing + demo

Perfect — locking Thu Jul 8, 14:00–15:00 PDT. I'll send the calendar invite from our side in a moment.

A few pre-call asks so we can size the session effectively:
- If possible, paste or attach the 5–10 minute representative request traces around peak (we'll look for tokenization variance and KV cache hit rates).
- Confirm whether scoring requests are synchronous HTTPS calls or pushed into a queue for workers. That changes latency budgeting and batching strategy.
- Any constraints on model variants (e.g., strict preference for a particular open model family, or openness to a quantized variant) — helps us recommend dedicated pool sizing.

Neha is looping in our Dedicated sizing specialist (Ben) on the call — he'll run through GPU pool footprint tradeoffs and burst options.

Thanks — see you Thu.

David
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-sizing-prep.pdf (sent earlier)

Thanks all — calendar invite accepted and sent from our side as well (you should see the shared event link). We uploaded the 5–10 minute representative trace file to the shared folder and included sampling around the 14:35 spike. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/fintro-traces

Quick answers to the pre-call asks:
- Scoring requests are synchronous HTTPS; we handle retries at the client layer.
- We're open to model variants but prefer to avoid experimental quantizations during initial rollout — prefer FP16 or known 4-bit profiles that you have verified.
- Our SLOs are strict on p99 (<=250ms) for scoring; batch jobs can tolerate longer windows.

If you want a one-page environment summary before the call, we can drop that in the shared folder; otherwise we'll walk through live.

See you Thu 14:00 PDT.

Best,
Liam
